paragraphs: Friend, here's what James is teaching: your life is a mist, so hold your plans loosely. The planners in James 4:13 had the whole year mapped out, but James says, "You do not even know what will happen tomorrow!" (James 4:14). His fix is simple. Say, "If the Lord is willing, we will live and do this or that" (James 4:15), because planning is fine and boasting in your plans is the problem (James 4:16).

Then James gets personal about what you do with what you know. "Anyone, then, who knows the right thing to do, yet fails to do it, is guilty of sin" (James 4:17). That one lands on ME. I know the right thing, I know it WELL, and I still stare at it like it's going to wash itself. So the question for you today is not what you know. It's what you will DO with it.

The warning to the rich comes from the same place. Their riches rotted, their gold and silver corroded, and the wages they held back from the harvesters were crying out, and "the ears of the Lord of Hosts" heard it (James 5:2-4). I think James wants you to see that stuff can't hold you up, and that how you treat the people who work for you matters to God. So hold your plans loosely, hold your treasure loosely, and pay people what they've earned.
